nodes.text: 파열위험지표는 stress/strength로 정의되어야 하며, stress는 ΔPSS(심장주기 내 진폭·피로 관점)가 임상적으로 더 적합하다.
ΔPSS 기반 VI가 순간 최대 PSS 기반 VI보다 임상적 기준(7개)의 부호 일치성 및 예측력에서 우수하다.
ΔPSS의 우수성은 맥동성(피로·진폭) 효과를 반영하므로 맥동성 FSI 시뮬레이션이 필요하다.
파열위험 지표 정의에는 strength(재료물성)를 분모로 넣어 정규화하는 것이 필요하며, 정규화 지수 α에 따라 민감도와 특성이 달라진다.
strength를 분모로 포함하는 VI 후보들(stress/strength^α) 가운데 α 값에 따라 민감도 순위와 임상기준 부합성이 변한다.
제안된 최종 VI 두 가지는 VI1 = ΔPSS / E_FC^{0.5} 및 VI2 = ΔPSS / E_FC^{1.0}으로, 7개 임상기준을 모두 만족한다.
전역 민감도 분석(Sobol) 결과 재료물성(material)이 혈류역학·형태학보다 파열위험 분산을 더 많이 설명한다 (Material > Hemodynamics > Morphology).
그룹화된 Sobol 지수에서 Material 그룹의 1차 및 전차 지수(S1, ST)가 Hemodynamics·Morphology 그룹보다 크다(두 표현형·두 VI에서 일관됨).
개별 입력 변수 수준에서 상위 결정인자는 E_vessel, E_FC, SBP, PP로 확인되었다(상위 4인자).
비용효율적 맥동성 FSI와 Gaussian Process 대리모델을 결합하면 대규모 입력공간에서 실용적으로 전역 민감도 분석을 수행할 수 있다.
LAP(784)와 CP(727) 유효 샘플로 학습된 GPR 대리모델은 5-fold 교차검증 기준에서 LAP VI1 R²=0.93 RMSE=0.07, CP VI1 R²=0.90 RMSE=0.09 등 우수한 예측 성능을 보였다.
대리모델을 이용한 Sobol 추정(1e5 샘플)은 원시 FSI 직접평가 대비 약 1000배 이상의 비용 절감으로 수초 내 평가가 가능했다.

Cost-effective pulsatile fluid-structure interaction (FSI) pipeline used to generate simulation outputs (pressure/velocity, solid displacement/stress time series) for idealized plaque phenotypes (LAP: 3 domains; CP: 4 domains). Uses boundary conditions and driving waveforms from elastance.dat and inflow.dat. Time integration Δt=1 ms; quadratic tetrahedral solid elements (mean element size 0.05 mm); convergence tol rel-residual 1e-4.
Finite-element setup for solid domain: quadratic tetrahedral elements, mean element size 0.05 mm; mesh independence verified (PSS change 6% 0.1->0.05 mm; 2% 0.05->0.025 mm).
Apply boundary conditions and driving waveforms from provided files (elastance.dat, inflow.dat) and documented BCs (bc.md).

Postprocess FSI time-series to compute PSS fields (maximum principal stress σ1 on fibrous cap surface) and ΔPSS = max_t σ1(t) - min_t σ1(t). Compute spherical/surface-averaged metrics using equal-area nodal partition.
Design-of-experiments: sample input parameter space (morphology, hemodynamics, material) according to input.csv to produce simulation cases (1,000-case design space; valid pairs later filtered).

Form six candidate vulnerability indices VI = stress / strength^α (two stress measures: PSS, ΔPSS; three α scenarios) and evaluate each candidate against seven pre-specified clinical sign criteria (sign/antisign consistency). Select candidates satisfying all seven criteria.

Train Gaussian Process Regression surrogates mapping inputs → selected VI outputs. Matern 5/2 kernel with ARD length-scales, log-marginal-likelihood maximization for hyperparameters, noise alpha fixed at 1e-6, inputs/outputs z-score normalized. 5-fold cross-validation used for model assessment. Implementation: scikit-learn 1.3.0 GPR on CPU (8 cores).
5-fold cross-validation to compute R² and RMSE for surrogate models and calibration (coverage of 95% prediction intervals).

Compute Sobol global sensitivity indices (first-order S1 and total ST) using Monte Carlo evaluation (1e5 samples) on trained GPR surrogates for group-level (Material/Hemo/Morpho) and individual-parameter indices.
Boundary condition and method documentation for the cost-effective FSI solver

Inflow driving waveform time series

FSI simulation outputs (PSS fields, FFR trends, rupture-location index) are consistent with literature trends and mesh-independence tests indicate acceptable discretization error (PSS changes 6% then 2%).
Evaluation of six candidate VIs against seven clinical sign criteria yielded two candidates (VI1, VI2) that satisfy all criteria.
GPR surrogate cross-validation performance: LAP VI1 R²=0.93 RMSE=0.07; CP VI1 R²=0.90 RMSE=0.09; prediction-interval coverage LAP 94%, CP 92%.
Grouped Sobol indices show Material group explains more variance (S1 and ST) than Hemodynamics or Morphology across phenotypes and selected VIs.
Individual-parameter Sobol indices identify top drivers E_vessel, E_FC, SBP, PP across phenotypes and selected VIs.
Sobol sensitivity indices (variance-based decomposition) quantify contribution of input parameters/groups to output variance; higher S1/ST indicates greater influence.
Gaussian process regression with ARD Matern kernels provides smooth probabilistic surrogates and enables low-cost MC evaluation for sensitivity analysis when trained and validated appropriately.

ΔPSS (stress amplitude / peak-to-peak) better captures fatigue/accumulated cyclic damage mechanisms than instantaneous peak stress, so it is a more relevant stress metric for rupture prediction under pulsatile loading.

edges.rationale: ΔPSS 기반 VI가 PSS 기반 VI보다 임상 기준과 예측성능에서 우수함을 보여주므로 stress로 ΔPSS를 택하는 주장을 직접 지지한다.
ΔPSS의 해석이 맥동성(진폭/피로)에 의존하므로 맥동성 FSI의 필요성을 논증해 ΔPSS를 stress로 선택하는 근거를 보강한다.
정규화 지수 α에 따른 VI 거동 변화는 strength 정규화의 필요성과 그 민감성을 입증한다.
실제 데이터에서 α별 후보 중 두 가지(α=0.5,1.0)가 모든 임상기준을 만족한 결과는 strength 정규화의 적용 가능성과 구체적 권고를 제공한다.
그룹별 Sobol 지수에서 Material 우위가 관찰되어 '재료물성이 지배적'이라는 주장을 직접 지지한다.
개별 변수 수준에서 E_vessel·E_FC·SBP·PP가 상위 지표로 도출된 것은 어떤 입력들이 Material·Hemo 그룹 내에서 실제로 분산을 주도하는지를 명시적으로 보여준다.
대리모델의 교차검증 성능은 대리모델 기반 민감도 분석의 신뢰성을 보장하므로 방법론적 실현 가능성을 지지한다.
대리모델을 사용한 계산비용 절감과 대규모 샘플 평가 가능성은 전역 민감도 분석 수행의 실용적 근거가 된다.
Grouped Sobol CSVs show Material group S1/ST larger than Hemodynamics and Morphology across LAP/CP and VI1/VI2, indicating material dominance of output variance.
Group-level Sobol indices directly quantify S1 and ST for Material vs other groups in the provided grouped Sobol data.
Individual-parameter Sobol CSVs identify E_vessel, E_FC, SBP, PP as the highest S1/ST contributors across phenotypes and VIs.
Reported 5-fold CV metrics (R², RMSE, calibration) demonstrate surrogate predictive performance for LAP and CP models as required for surrogate-based sensitivity analysis.
Candidate-evaluation method produced two VIs (VI1 and VI2) that satisfied all seven clinical sign criteria according to the selection procedure.
Simulation outputs including time-resolved stress fields and mesh-independence validation support the need to capture pulsatile/fatigue effects (ΔPSS) via pulsatile FSI.
Postprocessed PSS and ΔPSS fields from FSI simulations provide the stress measures used to construct VI candidates.
Evaluation of candidate VIs against seven clinical criteria found ΔPSS-based candidates perform better than alternatives in sign-consistency and selection, supporting ΔPSS superiority.
Reported GPR cross-validation metrics and calibration support the claim that GPR surrogates were effective for downstream Sobol analysis.
Grouped Sobol data directly show Material group's S1/ST exceed those of other groups in provided CSVs for both phenotypes and VIs.
Individual Sobol indices show which parameters (E_vessel, E_FC, SBP, PP) drive variance, supporting material dominance claim.
Candidate-evaluation results demonstrate that varying α changes candidate behavior and selection outcome, indicating sensitivity of VI properties to strength-normalization exponent.

figures.generation_prompt: Create a grouped vertical bar chart (aspect ratio 16:9) that shows grouped first-order (S1) and total-effect (ST) Sobol indices for two groups: LAP/CP and VI1/VI2. X-axis: four grouped categories in this order: LAP, CP, VI1, VI2 (each group label centered under its two bars). For each category draw two adjacent bars: S1 (left) and ST (right). Y-axis: Sobol index (unit: fraction 0–1); set tick marks at regular intervals but do NOT invent values — plot the exact numeric S1 and ST values from the author's sobol_grp CSV files. Order the groups left-to-right as listed above. Use a high-contrast, colorblind-safe palette: S1 = dark blue, ST = orange; include a legend in the top-right labeling the colors and "S1" and "ST". Place value annotations above each bar showing the exact numeric value from the data (if a value is missing, display the clear placeholder text "VALUE_MISSING"). Add a single annotation callout highlighting the largest ST across the four groups (pointing to the bar) with the text "largest ST". Style: clean academic vector style, white background, sans-serif font, thin gridlines only on the y-axis, no 3D effects or decorative elements. Use ONLY the author's real values from sobol_grp CSV; do not invent numbers.
